A posteriori error estimation

Source: R/error-estimation.R
estimate_error.Rd

estimate_error() computes the residual-based error estimator for a linear elliptic solution:

Usage

estimate_error(solution, diffusion_gradient = NULL)

Arguments

solution

A pde_solution of an elliptic_problem().

diffusion_gradient

Optional exact gradient of a scalar diffusion coefficient, function(x, y) returning a two-column matrix.

Value

A list of class pde_error_estimate with eta (per element), total, and the interior and edge contributions.

Details

eta_T^2 = h_T^2 ||f - c u_h - b . grad u_h + div(k grad u_h)||_T^2 + 1/2 sum_{interior E in T} h_E ||[k grad u_h . n]||_E^2 + sum_{Neumann/Robin E in T} h_E ||g - alpha u_h - k grad u_h . n||_E^2 + sum_{Dirichlet E in T} h_E ||d/ds (g_D - u_h)||_E^2.

Edges with no condition are zero-flux Neumann edges. An edge under any Dirichlet condition is a Dirichlet edge (as in the solver), and natural conditions on the same edge add up. The Dirichlet term measures how well the space represents the boundary data (tangential derivative by central differences). The diffusion coefficient in the flux jumps is evaluated on each side of an edge separately, so coefficients that jump across element edges are handled; finite-element coefficients are allowed. For P1 with constant diffusion the divergence term vanishes; variable scalar diffusion contributes grad k . grad u_h, computed with central differences of k with a step of 1e-3 times the inradius of each element, so the differences stay inside the element (pass diffusion_gradient for an exact gradient). Region coefficients (region_coefficient()) are constant on each element and contribute nothing. The estimator is reliable and efficient up to constants for diffusion-dominated problems (Verfurth 2013); it is not robust for strongly advection-dominated problems.

References

Verfurth, R. (2013). A Posteriori Error Estimation Techniques for Finite Element Methods. Oxford University Press.

Examples

mesh <- pde_mesh_rectangle(nx = 8)
sol <- solve_pde(poisson_problem(mesh, source = 1, boundary = dirichlet_bc(0)))
est <- estimate_error(sol)
est
#> <pde_error_estimate> total 0.2269 over 128 elements (max 0.03453)
